Preface
1 Preface
The following documentation provides you with all information re-
quired to to carry out maintenance and repair works on your HI-
SCAN 150 MPI X-Ray unit.
This document does not, however, deal with the detection of ob-
jects in X-Ray sequences.
We recommend that you read these instructions through carefully.
In particular, please be sure to read the section entitled "Safety",
which contains important information concerning your safety when
operating the unit.
The products of Smiths Detection are developed and manufac-
tured in compliance with the essential health and safety require-
ments of the European Union (EU).
1.1 Customer service
You receive technical support regarding your product from the loc-
al representative or from our company.
A quick service will be facilitated, if you can include the following
information with your request:
• contact partner in case of questions 
• telephone- and fax number of the contact partner
• type and serial number of the unit
• description of the troubles
1.2 Target group
This assembly instructions for partly completed machinery is ad-
dressed to persons/companies who are entrusted to incorporate
the HI-SCAN 150 MPI X-ray unit in a final machinery. Moreover,
this document includes important instructions for the user.

2.1 Conventions
2.1.1 Danger  categories
The safety instructions in this manual are subdivided into three
danger categories. These categories differ with regard to the
severity of injuries that can result from the non-compliance with the
instructions:
DANGER
Indicates a directly threatening danger. Non-compli-
ance leads to the most severe injuries or death!
WARNING
Indicates a possibly dangerous situation. Non-compli-
ance can lead to the most severe injuries or death!
CAUTION
Indicates a possibly dangerous situation. Non-compli-
ance can lead to slight or minor injuries!

2.2 Due diligence
The owner/user has to ensure that only duly trained personnel are
authorized to operate the HI-SCAN 150 MPI X-Ray unit. The oper-
ators’ state of knowledge is to be verified at regular intervals and, if
required, refresher training courses have to be carried out.
Please note that the exposure of human beings to X-radiation may
be harmful. The safe operation of the HI-SCAN 150 MPI X-Ray
unit is entirely your responsibility as the owner/user, and Smiths
assumes no liability relating to the use or operation of the equip-
ment, by you or anybody acting on your behalf.

Legal and official regulations
2.3 Legal and official regulations
Before you install and operate the HI-SCAN 150 MPI X-Ray unit, it
is critical that you, as the owner/user, must ensure full compliance
with all applicable laws and regulations, including without limitation,
applicable radiation protection regulations and accident prevention
regulations. Possible variations or changes of applicable laws
and/or regulations must always be considered. 
In addition, you may be required by applicable law to perform a ra-
diation protection check or an acceptance test after the installation
of the HI-SCAN 150 MPI X-Ray unit. You may be required to re-
peat such radiation protection checks or acceptance tests of the
HI-SCAN 150 MPI X-Ray unit at specific intervals or if you move
the HI-SCAN 150 MPI X-Ray unit to a different location.
DISCLAIMER:
Smiths Detection assumes no responsibility for the completeness
of the information provided above. It is your responsibility to en-
sure that the equipment is used and operated in full compliance
with Smiths Detection maintenance procedures and user guides. It
is your responsibility to ensure that the equipment is used and op-
erated in full compliance with the requirements of all applicable en-
vironmental or occupational health and safety laws, radiation
safety laws and industry standards relating to radiation safety for
personnel security screening systems using X-rays. It is your re-
sponsibility to operate the equipment within the radiation dose lim-
its established by such laws and standards. 
In addition you, as the owner/user must ensure that the designated
installation area complies with the requirements for the Conditions
of Use set out below.

2.8 Radiation protection regulations
The Hi-SCAN 150 X-Ray unit has been designed to comply with

Safety
3 Safety
The Hi-SCAN 150 X-Ray unit has been designed according to
state-of-the-art standards and in compliance with approved safety-
related regulations. When using the Hi-SCAN 150 X-Ray unit, risks
to life and limb of the user or third parties, or damage to the Hi-
SCAN 150 X-Ray unit and other material may nevertheless occur.
• Only use the Hi-SCAN 150 MPI X-Ray unit when in a technic-
ally perfect condition, and only use as intended and with due
awareness of safety and risks, and in compliance with these in-
structions.
• In case of malfunctions or changes of the operationalbehaviour
of the Hi-SCAN 150 MPI X-Ray unit, shut down the system and
have the malfunctions corrected.
• Before using the Hi-SCAN 150 MPI X-Ray unit the correct func-
tion of the emergency-stop system and the interlock circuit has
to be checked. Only operate the unit with a correct functional
safety system.
• Only operate the Hi-SCAN 150 MPI X-Ray unit when the tunnel
openings are covered in a manner that X-radiation cannot exit
the tunnel openings (e.g. with led curtains). Always adhere to
the radiation safety protocols.
3.1 Intended use
The Hi-SCAN 150 X-Ray unit is a transmission X-ray inspection
system for the inspection of bulk goods and material streams.
The intended use also includes observing of the following informa-
tion:
• The present Assembly instructions for partly completed ma-
chinery and the Technical Manual
• All referenced documents, in particular the safety instructions
• Technical data and environmental conditions

INFORMATION
The functionality of the Hi-SCAN 150 X-Ray unit can
only be guaranteed as long as the unit is operated in a
manner described in this documentation. Smiths Detec-

use!
3.1.1 Reasonably  foreseeable misuse
The components of the Hi-SCAN 150 MPI X-Ray unit may not be
used for purposes other than those described in this document and
in the referenced product documents. This includes among other
things:
• It is not allowed to use the Hi-SCAN 150 MPI X-Ray unit to
screen people or animals.
• The installation and use of software or software components
other than those belonging to the scope of delivery of the Hi-
SCAN 150 X-Ray unit is prohibited.
3.2 Structural alterations and spare
parts
Alterations and reconstructions can compromise the operational
safety of the Hi-SCAN 150 MPI X-Ray unit. Alterations and recon-
structions are generally forbidden. Any modification done without a
prior written consent of Smiths Detection will cause the loss of CE
declaration of conformity or the declaration of incorporation.
The following interventions, except for the works described in this
documentation, are not allowed without prior written consent of
Smiths Detection.
• Open and demount components
• Replace components
• Unauthorized structural alterations of components
• Program changes to the programmable control system
The Hi-SCAN 150 MPI X-Ray unit may only be modified or conver-
ted by personnel of Smiths Detection itself, by a service agent ap-

proved by the company, or by personnel authorised and trained by
the company. 
Only Smiths Detection's own staff, or a service centre or staff au -

SCAN 150 MPI X-Ray unit.
Original spare parts and accessories are specially designed for the
Hi-SCAN 150 MPI X-Ray unit. The installation or use of parts not

3.3 Safety devices
The Hi-SCAN 150 MPI X-Ray unit has several safety measures:
• Interlock switches
• Branch connection for an external emergency-stop signal
• X-Ray On indicators
3.3.1 Interlock  switches
Two interlock switches are located behind the security cover a of
the collimator. In case the security cover is removed or not
tightened correctly the interlock switches are opened. 
Two interlock switches are located at the flap of the detectorline
box. In case the cover of the detector line box is not closed and
tightened correctly the interlock switches are opened.
3.3.2 External  emergency‐stop signal
The safety system also monitors an external emergency stop sig-
nal which can be looped in via the interface block =REJ+900-X3.
In case that the emergency stop signal is applied:

Remaining risks
3.5 Remaining risks
3.5.1 X ‐Rays
Individuals being exposed to X-rays can suffer damage from ex -
posure to radiation. The possibility of harm occurring depends on
the following factors: 
• Distance to the radiation source
• Duration of stay within the radiation area
• Shielding 
The installation and operation of the Hi-SCAN 150 MPI X-Ray unit
must have been notified to the competent authority by the operat-
ing company and possibly been approved by the authority!
 Before putting the Hi-SCAN 150 MPI X-Ray unit into service;
• familiarise yourself with the relevant radiation protection rules
• verify that the unit is free of damages that may affect the
safety of the inspection process.
• verify the correct system set-up (position of the operator
desk, correct position of the shielding walls)
• perform a radiation survey whenever in doubt.
 Never put the Hi-SCAN 150 MPI X-Ray unit into service, if any 
components are damaged.
 The operator needs to ensure that all required operating ele-
ments (e.g.: Interlock switches) are functional before an inspec-
tion is carried out.
 Never remove or modify any components. This applies in partic-
ular to covers and all safety devices (e.g. interlock switches, 
sealed screws) 
 Replacement of components to the safety circuitry may only be 
supplied by Smiths Detection!
16 95595532 -30.01.2015- Smiths Detection

Safety
 In case of damage to interlock switches and sealed screws on 
covers: Immediately take the X-ray inspection unit out of service
and have the damage repaired. 
95595532 -30.01.2015- Smiths Detection 17

Remaining risks
3.5.2 Electric  current
Various components (e.g. connection terminals) carry dangerously
high voltages.
On cable ducts, cable insulation can be damaged.
Electric shock risk particularly in the following situations:
• Removing panel covers
• Opening electric terminal boxes
• Touching parts which carry voltage due to faults
• Touching damaged cables.
 Have the electrical equipment checked regularly.
Operation
 Do not modify safety devices.
 Immediately repair loose connections or scorched cables.
Maintenance
 Observe the following measures prior to repair works on the Hi-
SCAN 150 MPI X-Ray unit
• Inform operating personnel.
• De-energize the corresponding components and secure
against switching on again.
 With uninterruptible power supply (UPS) (optional): Be aware 
that after switching off the Hi-SCAN 150 MPI X-Ray unit com-
ponents may still be energized.
• Check de-energized state.
• Ground and short-circuit components. 
• Insulate and enclose neighbouring live components.
18 95595532 -30.01.2015- Smiths Detection

Safety
• Attach warning sign: "Do not switch on! Work being per-
formed on the electrical equipment."
• Use original fuses with the prescribed amperage only.
• Defects such as loose connections or scorched cables, must
be repaired immediately.
• Use insulated tools only.
• Use measuring equipment with protected measuring lines
only.
 After any modification, maintenance or repair during which ener-
gized components are replaced or repaired, you have to check

The technician carrying out the installation, maintenance or re-
pair is responsible for compliance with rules and regulations

If national laws and regulations are unknown or do not exist, the
following tests should be carried out in any case:
• Visual inspection of all safety-relevant features of the unit.
• Check the labels
• Measurement of the line voltage, and comparison with the
type plate on the unit.

ors and keyboard is routed neatly.
3.5.4 Danger  of cutting and crushing
Installation, transportation, maintenance
When attaching or removing any covers or panels, there is a risk of
hand cutting.

Remaining risks
When bringing in or removing the transport dollies underneath a
section frame during transportation there is a risk of finger crushing.
 Wear protective gloves during maintenance and installation 
works
When opening the flap of the detector line box compartment the
heavy flap can glide out of someones hand.
 Always use two people to open or close the flap of the detector-
line box compartment.
 Wear protective gloves
 Secure an opened flap with the two safety catches.
3.5.5 Heavy  weights
Operation, installation and maintenance
During installation and maintenance works, lifting heavy parts, like
the generator section, tunnel section, conveyor section, X-Ray
generator can lead to back injuries. 
 Take care when lifting heavy parts and always burden your 
knees and unburden your back
 Wear shoes with steel toe caps when lifting the test stand
 Always adhere to your local heavy lifting guidelines and prac-
tices to avoid the risk of back injury.
 Always use one or more persons when handling with heavy 
weights.

3.6 Avoidance of material damage
3.6.1 Reject  distribution
ATTENTION
Only connect reject valves with free-wheeling diode.
3.6.2 X ‐Ray generator
 If the X-ray generator of the HI-SCAN 150 MPI X-Ray unit has 
not been operated for more than 6 months, you have to regen-
erate the generator, i.e. run it in with reduced high tension!
 Do not under any circumstances, not even for a short time, op-
erate the generators at 160kV, because you might destroy the 
X-ray tube! In such cases, disconnect the generator cable(s) 
from the generator / from all generators before you switch on 
the X-ray unit!

System description
4 System  description
The HI-SCAN 150 MPI X-Ray unit uses transmission X-radiation
technology to inspect bulk goods and material streams and to sort
them by pneumatic reject valves. (The reject valves are not part of
the delivery). Bulk goods and material streams pass across an X-
Ray beam through the use of a conveyor. (Conveyor is not part of
the HI-SCAN 150 MPI X-Ray unit).
The HI-SCAN 150 MPI X-Ray unit consists of several compart-
ments  (see Fig. 7).

Pre start-up checks
7 Pre  start‐up checks
Before turning on the HI-SCAN 150 MPI X-Ray unit the operator
should carry out the below pre start-up checks.
 1: Panel housing is not damaged.
 2: All flaps and doors are closed.
 3: Ensure that the tunnel openings are covered in a manner that
X-radiation cannot exit the tunnel openings (e.g. with led cur-
tains).
 4: Last operation
• Verify, if the HI-SCAN 150 MPI X-Ray unit has been oper-
ated within the last 6 month. If you are unsure of when the HI-
SCAN 150 MPI X-Ray unit was last operated, ask a qualified
service technician to check the log files of the unit.
CAUTION
Do not switch on the X-Ray generators, if they have not
been operated for a period of 6 months! Instead, deac-
tivate the unit's X-ray systems until the regeneration of
the X-ray generators has been carried out by a qualified
service technician!

Check housing panels
Check all the outer housing panels of the unit for visibly damage.  
 Replace damaged side and top panels in order to avoid injuries,
unauthorized access and soiling of the unit. 
 Repair damaged or loose sheet suspensions or hinges or re-
place such parts.
 Replace or complete scratched or missing labels.
30 95595532 -30.01.2015- Smiths Detection

Maintenance
Carry out safety check
All safety measures must be checked if they are intact.
 Check the unit for defects on the lead shielding such as missing
shielding plates on the detector lines or on the X-ray generat-
ors, missing screws or rivets or damaged lead foil.
 Check the unit for mechanical damages on cables and electric 
and electronic modules.
 Carry out a leakage radiation test (F Fehler: Referenz nicht ge-
funden).
 Check the function of the protective bonding circuit.
Check PE wiring
Ensure that all elements of the unit are grounded correctly. Use an
ohmmeter to check the PE wiring.
 Check the PE wire between the mains connector and the unit 
main distribution. 
 Check the PE protection to the housing panels, unit frame and 
other earthed unit parts.
Check emergency stop switches (external)
Ensure that all external emergency-stop buttons are functioning
correctly (F 13).
 Check, if the unit can be switched off by each of the available 
emergency stop switches.
Check interlock system
With the unit switched off, interrupt an interlock switch by removing
or opening the respective leaded sheet (e.g. torso detector line box
cover).

Troubleshooting
10 Troubleshooting
